title: The Third Man - musical thriller at The Menier - review
transcript: hello welcome to theater reviews with Paul sa I'm here at the menia Chocolate Factory to see the third man theater has become something of a vampire in recent years roaming the dark auditori of Cinemas searching for films to turn into musicals Groundhog Day is newly opened at the Old Vic a version of Brokeback Mountain with music can be seen at SoHo Place 42nd Street the wizard of O Sunset Boulevard and Greece are all back this year just doubt fires on the way and of course there are the old favorites Back to the Future Mulan Rouge and The Lion King but one film I never expected to be adapted as a stage musical is the third man yet here it is at London's maner Chocolate Factory and it's a Triumph keep watching and I'll tell you why but first if you find my reviews useful Please Subscribe it'll help my channel grow and you'll be the first to hear about my future reviews I have a slight reservation about one aspect of the adaptation of the third man but it's far outweighed by the thrilling Pace in the roller coaster emotions wisely it sticks closely to Graham Green's original mystery story of love and betrayal with its reluctant hero its twists and turns and its shocks I'll try not to give too much away because you may not have seen this classic black and white film from 1949 let's start with the music written by George Fenton among the 100 plus films and TV series for which he's written the score or Gandy You've Got Mail the jewel in the crown and David atra's Planet series appropriate to a serious story his music leans towards the drama of Cloe Michelle sherberg L miserabl or the starkness of Kurt Val's threy Opera rather than say the nostalgic lushness of Lloyd Weber or the easy listen Melodies of Alan Menin but Mr Fenton is a brave man to tackle the third man because the film's theme is one of the most famous ever written in this musical version he pays brief homage to the jangling ziver based hit but goes for a score that suggests danger passion and anger play by live nine-piece Orchestra the songs enhance the story and reveal character as they should in a good musical the legendary Dom black and Christopher Hampton who are jointly credited with the book add some sharp lyrics There are even a couple of Duets that Rogers and Hammerstein would have been proud of the story is about a Pulp Fiction writer called Holly Martin played by Sam Underwood who arrives in Vienna at the end of World War II and it's occupied by American British and Russian soldiers he's there to do some work for an old school friend Harry lime only to find he's died in an accident as the First Act progresses he becomes increasingly suspicious about the circumstances s surrounding his friend's death the British military police meanwhile indicate to him that lime was a bad lot the First Act ends with an astonishing Discovery and the show continues with even more shocking revelations and heightened drama where the musical really stands out is in the feelings expressed by Holly and also by lime's lover Anna both loved Harry and can't believe he would have been involved in anything truly bad as the pair investigate Harry's death Holly falls in love with Anna and pursues her with puppy-like devotion a sentiment she does not return the production is blessed with a star in Sam Underwood who's able to communicate the complex character of Holly through both his singing and his acting in many ways he's a hero straight out of one of his own adventure novels but in this story although he's the lead character Holly is a natural follower rather than a leader and Mr Underwood conveys his innocence as well as the sadness frustration and infatuation he feels not to mention his naive determination Natalie Dunn is strong as Anna and by dwelling on her more than is the case in the film The Musical is able to show her in the nightclub singing songs that could have come straight out of the threy Opera or indeed cavaret songs both sad and amusing and indicative of her freethinking character and because we get to know her the subplot of the almost romantic triangle between Holly Anna and Harry carries more weight Simon Bailey also impresses as a feelingless villain who commands devotion uh and that is my reservation about the adaptation he's portrayed as more obviously nasty and not as full of fake charm as this key character was in the film Edward Baker Julie and Jonathan Andrew Hume strike just the right note as the righteous but ruthless military policeman major callow and Sergeant Payne other characters are more in the way of caricatures but they are well acted it's a pleasure to see Derek Griffiths as the Porter and then there's Rachel Eisen as his wife Gary Milner Alan vickory and Harry Morrison as lime's Shady Associates the design by Paul Farnsworth is full of atmosphere the costumes in Gray or other subdued colors add to the film Noir effect Rubble litters the edges of the stage floor a dark alley or tunnel goes off to the side you feel you are in a Sinister City ravaged by War the menu has been reconfigured so the audience is on three sides and actors run up and down the aisles ramping up the excitement and thank goodness the sight lines are kept free from obstruction the simplest of furniture is enough to suggest effectively a hotel lounge backstage at the nightclub a flat and even a ferris wheel gond getting us off to the best of starts is the opening scene where Holly wanders the dimly lit streets of Vienna at night help by dark expressionist lighting from Emma Chapman and is surrounded by people begging straight away we know we are in desperate times it's a masterpiece of Direction by Trevor nun who brings so much that he learned and practiced in a long career that encompasses slay misera cats and the National Theater production of Oklahoma he constantly Keeps Us gripped with a changing Pace that switches from frenetic activity to tense conversation credit to Christopher Hampton whose previous plays and translations include Lon Don's art Sunset Boulevard and Florian zeelas the father I thought a musical adaptation of the third man couldn't be done but Christopher Hampton and his team have done it I give the third man at the maner Chocolate Factory four stars I hope you enjoyed this review and found it useful uh if you did why not subscribe to my channel Channel and you'll be the first to know about my future reviews or you can read my reviews at theater. reviews and why not follow me on Twitter Instagram and Facebook thanks for watching
